crew_field_steps: FIRST: follow ONE entire attached many-raceme panicle on the living vaseygrass tuft (species gallery index 9), then examine the separate full flowering-axis image (index 0). Commonly about 10–20 unilateral racemes, but branch count overlaps dallisgrass.

SECOND: examine the actual lifted purple-sheathed crown and connected fibrous roots (gallery index 7). This proves a real rooted base, NOT a measured underground rhizome nor a root-to-head continuous specimen.

THIRD: distinguish the photographed EXTERIOR sheath hairs (indices 6–8) and hairy node (index 3) from the TRUE INNER membranous ligule, which is still missing. Published ligule ranges vary (~3–5 mm in Kew GrassBase, ~3–9 mm VicFlora).

FOURTH: follow attached paired spikelets (index 2) to Harry Rose's labelled dissection (index 1): lower glume absent; upper glume, lower sterile lemma, firm upper fertile lemma and palea shown, but no calibrated ruler. Never label dark stigmas as awns.

FIFTH: compare one complete P. dilatatum panicle (index 5) and a matched mature 1-mm-scale spikelet pair: Vasey usually ~2–2.8 mm versus Dallis ~2.7–3.9 mm, with overlap; silky margins are shared. P. floridanum (index 10) is a different native-regional comparison, not proof of Hays nativity.
what_to_photograph_for_confirmation: OPEN TRUE INNER LIGULE: authenticated Vaseygrass blade peeled from sheath, adaxial free membrane in side light beside physical 1-mm ruler; exterior sheath hairs and node hairs must remain distinguishable.
MATURE SPIKELET PAIRS: five ripe paired spikelets attached on a single raceme, front/side views at 10–20× beside 1-mm ruler; resolve silky upper-glume margins.

DISSECTED MATURE ORGANS: same-plant spikelet opened at 20–40× showing absent lower glume, 3(–5)-veined upper glume, sterile lemma, firm fertile lemma and palea with scale; do not invent awns or a lower glume.
MATCHED LOOK-ALIKE: source-verified P. dilatatum complete flowering head and five mature spikelets photographed at the same orientation and scale, optionally P. pubiflorum.
OPTIONAL LAST-MILE: locally voucher-verified single rooted crown continuously traced to full flowering culm and measured short knotted rhizome; root crown itself already photographed.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Count branches on ONE complete culm, not overlapping heads. Contrast 2–3 mm spikelets under measured macro with 3–4 mm long-haired dallisgrass; do not key solely by abundance of racemes or overall height. Use Florida paspalum as another few-branch, large-spikelet look-alike.
do_not_use_alone: Number of racemes without the entire flowering axis
Habitat, height, or vegetative tuft in isolation
Microscopic glume hairs or spikelet length inferred from a photo without scale
comparisons.field_identification_note: Record full head with branch count and centimeter ruler; 5 mature spikelets face-on and on edge with millimeter scale; compare lower/upper glumes and silky hair margin. Same-plant rooted tuft and true collar still needed.

field_photo_quickcheck.heading: Vaseygrass — first PHOTO true clump/root, then true inner ligule, then spikelets
steps: Look at SAME species gallery panel 10 (index9) for true healthy leafy tuft with flowering panicle on connected stems in field. The roadside scene in panel 5 (index4) is a population view, not an isolated plant.

Actual fibrous ROOTS in Harry Rose basal image panel 8 (index7) connect to purple basal sheaths and the crown. No measured under-soil rhizome section, but unlike a stalk entering soil this genuinely establishes a rooted base.

Panels 7–9 (indices6–8) show authentic long OUTER lower leaf sheath hairs and purple surfaces. They DO NOT expose the triangular 3–5mm FREE INNER ligule. Node hair photo index3 is also not ligule; do not arrow or teach it as one.

Full flowering axis panel 1 (index0) shows MANY narrower separate racemes, whereas regionally native P. floridanum panel 11 (index10) has two prominent racemes; totals overlap, do not identify by count alone.

Real original labeled P. urvillei reproductive panel 2 (index1) shows upper glume, sterile lemma, hard fertile lemma and palea; photograph author labels already present. Source has no calibrated 1-mm ruler; identification still benefits from measured mature material.

Dallisgrass is DIFFERENT species panel 6 (index5) and also has silky glume margins. Compare longer/wider mature 3–4mm Dallisgrass spikelets against ~2–3mm Vasey under same scale rather than falsely using hairy margins alone.

Keep Harry Rose Commons CC BY2 credit/source, and separate David Stang P. floridanum CC BY-SA4 and Joey Santore CC BY-NC conditional noncommercial rights. Photo pixels and new 4 broad arrows verified; site Pages/mobile QA pending.
field_photo_quickcheck.field_rule: Use whole plant+flowering stalk+authentic rooted fibrous crown, paired mature spikelets and REAL glume parts; only call the ligule visible when it is the opened inner blade-sheath membrane, not basal sheath hairs or a hairy node.
field_photo_quickcheck.warning: 11 gallery panels = nine exact source *P. urvillei* local JPEGs plus one *P. dilatatum* and one *P. floridanum* look-alike, both separately identified different species. No actual true inner ligule photo, no same-scale ripe comparison. No local Hays specimen from Australian photo.

field_id_finish_pass.field_recognition: VASEYGRASS: follow the complete many-raceme, one-sided flowering axis of a living leafy perennial tuft (real gallery panel index 9) and the photographed attached fibrous root crown (index 7). Mature paired spikelets usually ~2–2.8 mm; compare Dallisgrass ~2.7–3.9 mm at equal scale because sizes and raceme counts overlap. Photographer-labelled dissection (index 1) shows upper glume, sterile lemma, firm fertile lemma and palea; lower glume is absent, and no long awn is present. Published true INNER membranous ligule is still unphotographed: exterior purple sheath hairs (indices 6–8) and node hairs (3) do NOT show it.
field_id_finish_pass.lookalike_separation: Count branches on ONE complete culm, not overlapping heads. Contrast 2–3 mm spikelets under measured macro with 3–4 mm long-haired dallisgrass; do not key solely by abundance of racemes or overall height. Use Florida paspalum as another few-branch, large-spikelet look-alike.

measured_diagnostic_key_20261022.measured_diagnostic: Robust perennial tuft; membranous ligule approximately 3–5 mm in GrassBase; paired spikelets approximately 2–2.8 mm; lower glume absent or obscure, upper glume silky-margined, awns absent.
measured_diagnostic_key_20261022.local_lookalikes: Dallisgrass typically has fewer racemes and larger spikelets, with overlap; avoid diagnosing by head silhouette alone.
measured_diagnostic_key_20261022.last_mile_photo_arrow_gaps: Rooted plant, entire panicle, measured paired spikelets with glume/lemma dissection, true membranous ligule and matched dallisgrass.

lane4_20261023.science_correction: Smithsonian Flora Hawaiian Islands: 12–18 racemes usually (6–25), spikelets paired approximately 2.2–2.7 mm; ligule triangular 3–5 mm. FNA ranges broader (4–30 branches, ligules 1–4(7.7)mm). Both upper glume and lower sterile lemma show silky marginal hairs; long silky hairs are NOT unique to Dallisgrass.

species_anatomy_finalization_20261024.look_here_first: On ONE intact tall flowering culm, count the many slender one-sided racemes; then examine a mature paired spikelet with a 1-mm scale. A 2–2.8 mm, silky-edged spikelet with NO lower glume supports vaseygrass. Confirm the 3–5 mm membranous true ligule at the INNER blade–sheath junction; do not mistake basal sheath hairs for the ligule.
measured_structures: GROWTH: robust, tufted perennial; culms 80–250 cm in Kew GrassBase; basal leaf sheaths may be hairy. Rooted growth form is not confirmed by the existing wide seedhead photograph.
FLOWERING AXIS: commonly 10–20 unilateral racemes, each about 4–13 cm, distributed along a central axis about 10–20 cm; branches and spikelet rows must be counted on one connected inflorescence.

SPIKELETS: paired, ovate and dorsally compressed, 2–2.8 mm long in Kew; VicFlora includes 1.6–2.8 mm. One basal sterile floret and one upper fertile floret occur within each spikelet; the two adjacent spikelets are NOT two florets.
LOWER GLUME: absent or extremely reduced. Do not draw an arrow to an invented lower glume.
UPPER GLUME: approximately spikelet-length, thin, usually 3-veined (VicFlora permits 3–5), with conspicuous silky cilia on its margins and some surface hairs.
LOWER STERILE LEMMA: approximately spikelet-length, thin, generally 3-veined, often with silky marginal hairs; distinguish this actual lemma from the upper glume in a dissected mature spikelet.

UPPER FERTILE LEMMA: firm/hardened, pale, finely striate, rounded/obtuse at tip; 1.4–2.6 mm in AusGrass, versus 1.6–1.8 mm in Flora of New Zealand. The corresponding palea is firm and enclosed by the incurved lemma margins.
AWNS: no long projecting glume or fertile-lemma awn. Silky marginal hairs are NOT awns.
TRUE LIGULE: unfringed membranous tongue, about 3–5 mm in Kew GrassBase and 3–9 mm in VicFlora; inspect the inner collar separately from adjacent sheath-mouth hairs.
crew_sequence: 1. Photograph a rooted tuft with a complete, connected flowering culm; record the basal sheath hair pattern and any actual rhizome without inferring underground structures.
2. Count all unilateral racemes on that SAME panicle; do not sum several crossing seedheads.
3. Open the inner leaf collar and measure the free membranous ligule with a millimeter ruler; distinguish separate long basal sheath hairs.
4. At 10–20× photograph at least five ripe attached paired spikelets with a 1-mm scale; check the 2–2.8 mm range, shape and silky margin.
5. Dissect one ripe spikelet: identify absent lower glume, thin hairy upper glume, lower sterile lemma, hard upper fertile lemma and palea; mark each only if the pixels actually resolve it.
6. Compare with dallisgrass on the SAME scale: P. dilatatum generally has fewer racemes and larger 2.7–3.9 mm spikelets; size and branch counts overlap, so use multiple traits.
7. If spikelet parts and same-plant collar cannot be verified, retain Paspalum cf. urvillei rather than asserting a confirmed species ID.
local_lookalikes: Paspalum dilatatum (introduced dallisgrass): commonly fewer flowering racemes, spikelets typically 2.7–3.9 mm in AusGrass; silky upper-glume margins also occur, so hairs alone do NOT separate them.
Paspalum pubiflorum: also paired oval spikelets and several unilateral racemes; compare mature upper-glume hairs/veins, branch count and true collar rather than a single close-up row.
Sorghum halepense (introduced Johnsongrass): a branched open panicle with different paired sessile/pedicelled spikelet architecture, NOT the narrow unilateral rows of paired Paspalum spikelets.
needs_public_photo: ROOTED HABIT: source-verified vaseygrass with one connected root crown, basal sheaths and full mature flowering axis, centimeter ruler; avoid treating an isolated seedhead as evidence of perennial base.
TRUE LIGULE: same plant, inner blade–sheath junction opened, side lighting and 1-mm scale; show 3–5 mm membrane separately from basal hairs.
ATTACHED PAIRS: 10–20× ripe spikelets on one raceme, 1-mm scale, silk fringe and pairing resolvable.
DISSECTED PARTS: 20–40× upper glume (including veins), sterile lemma, hard fertile lemma and palea from one vouchered mature spikelet, mm scale; no invented lower-glume or awn arrows.
LOOK-ALIKE: P. dilatatum mature spikelets and intact head photographed at the same scale and orientation; optionally P. pubiflorum.
